clue.text: Outstanding leader uses regular carrier

parts.note: regular in the sense of normal or usual means standard
one who carries something is a bearer

explanation.surface: A top leader relies on a scheduled airline or transport firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding leader' is read as a prominent chief, and 'carrier' suggests an airline, but here it simply means one who bears something.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard-bearer carried the flag at the head of an army, hence a prominent leader of a cause or movement.

clue.text: Acrobat's supporter adjusts the top rig

indicators.note: to adjust is to rearrange, so the letters of the three words that follow are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A circus hand reconfigures the rigging at the top of the big top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusts' rearranges the nine letters of THE TOP RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-wire walker is held up by a taut rope strung between platforms.

clue.text: Steadfastness never wavers

indicators.note: something that wavers moves unsteadily, so the letters of the neighbouring word are shuffled

explanation.surface: Unwavering resolve, the clue claims, never falters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wavers' signals an anagram of NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve means courage or firmness of purpose under pressure, the quality of holding steady.

clue.text: Hors d'oeuvre could be approved shortly — see it is amended recipe

parts.note: app. is a short form of approved

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the letters gathered here are put in a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, the Latin 'take' heading a prescription

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether a starter would pass muster once the recipe is revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended' rearranges the letters of 'see it'; R for recipe is the Rx heading a prescription. 'could be' and 'is' are link words, and the kitchen 'recipe' is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: An hors d'oeuvre is a small dish served before the main meal to stimulate hunger, which is what a starter does.

clue.text: He gives university tutor an alternative

parts.note: a don is a fellow or tutor at a university such as Oxford or Cambridge
the word or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone offers an academic a choice of options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He gives' looks like the start of a sentence; it is the definition, someone who gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor who contributes money, blood or organs is one who gives.

clue.text: Initially every putt hit over most of the green is short

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second
initially picks the opening letter of each of the next three words
most of drops the final letter of the word for the green colour

parts.note: emerald is a vivid shade of green

explanation.surface: A golfer reflects that every putt struck past the hole fell short.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture makes 'green' the putting surface; it is the colour EMERALD, which 'most of' cuts to EMERAL. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral is fleeting or short-lived, lasting only a brief time.

clue.text: As a rule showers can be heard

indicators.note: can be heard says that the word for showers is said aloud to give a word that sounds the same

parts.note: showers of water from the sky are rain

explanation.surface: A forecaster notes that, as a rule, showers are audible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a rule' reads as 'usually', but it defines the noun: to rule is to reign.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period of their rule, so 'as a rule' is reign in a phrase sense.

clue.text: Animals take fish eggs before swamp grass turns up

indicators.note: before puts the fish-egg piece ahead of the next piece

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs of a fish

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the grass word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in marshes

explanation.surface: Creatures feed on fish spawn while marsh vegetation springs up around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses REED to DEER; 'take' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe deer are a small species of European deer, so they are animals.

clue.text: Notched up 20 to finish with 500

indicators.note: to finish with places the next piece at the end

parts.note: a score is twenty
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A batsman reached twenty and ended with five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers suggest cricket runs; SCORE is twenty and D is the Roman 500.
explanation.definitionFit: To have notched up points is to have scored them, as a tally is cut in a stick.

clue.text: Smoke starts to infiltrate gearbox in vehicle

indicators.note: in places the opening letters inside the word for a vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A smuggler's contraband begins to work its way into a car's gearbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' reads as a verb or a cloud of fumes, but it is the noun for something smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigar is something one smokes, and 'a smoke' is everyday slang for one.

clue.text: Judy's partner goes on-line: end of joke

parts.note: Punch is Judy's husband in the Punch and Judy puppet show
taken as written

explanation.surface: Judy's husband connects to the internet, which ends the comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show; 'goes on' is a link word, and the hyphen in 'on-line' is just surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The punchline is the closing sentence that delivers the humour of a gag.

clue.text: Quiet place for military bridge-builders to parley

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps that builds bridges
to treat is to negotiate or parley

explanation.surface: Army engineers seek a calm spot in which to negotiate.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers; 'treat' is used in its old sense of negotiating terms, as in 'treat with the enemy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a secluded refuge where one goes for peace and seclusion.

clue.text: The old Italian church affair

parts.note: an ancient inhabitant of Rome was a Roman
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Italian of olden times has a church connected with a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: CE is the Church of England; 'The' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair or amorous relationship.

clue.text: Not a good day to return flag

indicators.note: to return means the combined pieces are turned around and read backwards

parts.note: something not good is poor

explanation.surface: It is a bad day for bringing back the banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses POOR plus D. 'flag' looks like a banner but is the verb meaning to tire.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or wilt, which is what sagging plants and spirits do.

clue.text: Dabbles about, covering one eastern part of Staffordshire

indicators.note: covering means the outer word wraps around the inner pieces

parts.note: to potter about is to dabble aimlessly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone tinkers aimlessly while covering an eastern district of a Midlands county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts I and E inside POTTERS. The Potteries is the pottery-making area around Stoke-on-Trent in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potteries is the region of north Staffordshire famed for its ceramics industry.

clue.text: Hugely popular singer's terrific opening cut short

parts.note: super means terrific

indicators.note: cut short trims the final letter of the word for an opening

parts.note: a start is an opening or beginning

explanation.surface: A pop idol's brilliant debut performance was abruptly curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the last letter off START to leave STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstar is an extremely famous performer such as a pop singer.

clue.text: Motorised vessel with tangled bow-rope needs a tug to start

indicators.note: tangled suggests the rope's letters are knotted into a new arrangement
to start takes the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A motor launch whose mooring line is snarled needs towing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' rearranges BOWROPE into POWERBO; then A and the first letter of 'tug' ('to start'). 'needs' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerboat is a fast boat driven by an engine.

clue.text: What froglike creature uses to cultivate fungus?

parts.note: what belongs to a froglike creature is the toad's
an implement used to cultivate the soil is a tool

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what a frog-like animal works the soil with to grow mushrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'a toad's tool', the thing a toad would use to cultivate its garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A toadstool is a mushroom-shaped fruiting body, especially an inedible fungus.

clue.text: Fielder's inaccurate return brings defeat

explanation.surface: A fielder's wild throw costs his team the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an overthrow is a fielder's throw that misses the stumps and lets the batsmen run extra; 'brings' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a wayward throw past the wicket yields extra runs; as a verb, it means to topple or vanquish a ruler or regime.

clue.text: Cricket side freezes positions of responsibility

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
to ice something is to freeze it

explanation.surface: A cricket team freezes out those in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The off side is the half of a cricket field facing the batsman's bat.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a post or position of authority, so the plural means such posts.

clue.text: Inclined to have thin time

parts.note: lean means thin

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to have a sparse spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning means tilted or sloping, so having leaned is being inclined.

clue.text: Almost the finest city of Ancient Greece or Egypt

definitions.text: city of Ancient Greece or Egypt

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost removes the last letter of the phrase that follows

parts.note: the finest is the best

explanation.surface: A traveller ranks a classical city nearly the greatest in the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final T from THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: There were two ancient cities of this name, one in Boeotia and one on the Nile.

clue.text: Trapped between franc and yen, I'd become restless

indicators.note: trapped between means the pieces sit inside the two currency letters

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for franc
the apostrophe is ignored
to get is to become, as in get angry

explanation.surface: Stuck between currencies, a trader grows fidgety.
explanation.walkthrough: IDGET sits between F and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A fidgety person keeps moving nervously, unable to settle.

clue.text: Place for storage of French earthenware

parts.note: de is French for of
a pot is a vessel of earthenware

explanation.surface: A warehouse for French pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: DE is French for 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a warehouse or storehouse where goods are kept.

clue.text: Woody-stemmed American plant provides your cocoa, oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tropical shrub supplies your hot chocolate in an unusual way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the odd-numbered letters: Y, U from 'your' and C, C, A from 'cocoa'. 'provides' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a spiky-leaved plant native to the Americas with a woody trunk.

clue.text: To prise out a swift reply

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting something prised open is done with a quick comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TO PRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick retort, originally a fencer's counter-thrust.

clue.text: Every year 50% peruse what you're perusing now

parts.note: pa is short for per annum, Latin for each year

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half the next word, its first half

explanation.surface: Half your reading time each year goes on what you are reading now.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is per annum; '50%' takes the first half of 'peruse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The FT crossword is printed in a newspaper, which the solver is reading.

clue.text: Italian island firm goes round Channel Islands providing lively music

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples

indicators.note: goes round means the company abbreviation surrounds the islands abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An Italian island business circling the Channel Islands lays on cheerful tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lively music' sounds like a description of a firm's jingle; 'providing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a free, lively musical composition in a fanciful style.

clue.text: Quietly stood up for ordinary form of language

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
rose means stood up

explanation.surface: Someone quietly got to their feet in support of plain speech.
explanation.walkthrough: P is piano in music; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Prose is written or spoken language without metre, as opposed to verse.

clue.text: Was sitting in front of island plant holding one pound in an acceptable manner

indicators.note: in front of puts the sitting piece ahead of the rest

parts.note: sat means was sitting

indicators.note: holding means the plant word encloses the next pieces

parts.note: a factory is an industrial plant
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra

explanation.surface: A worker sat before an island factory that held a single pound in tolerable fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' means an industrial works, not a flower; FACTORY 'holding' I and L gives FACTORILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Done well enough to meet requirements means done adequately.
